acceptance: Crash before/after every submit/confirm/journal transition plus L1 rollback/configured-source inconsistency, including at least one rollback deeper than the configured finality depth proving the automated k-depth recovery of W13; no double submit, lost evidence, false verified state, manual-surgery recovery step, or stuck unrecoverable workflow.
focusedCommand: pnpm --dir demo/midgard-watcher exec vitest run tests/crash-rollback-matrix.test.ts

seams.journalBoundary: demo/midgard-watcher/src/durable-store.ts compareAndSwapWatcherDurableAtomicSnapshotV1 (the single atomic durable byte-replacement boundary)
seams.crashInjection: WatcherDurableAtomicBackend.compareAndSwap throws at an exact attempt index, before or after the durable byte replacement; the post-commit throw is the ambiguous window a real process crash produces
seams.recoveryProcedure: restart re-invokes the same deterministic driver against the same durable snapshot; no manual-surgery step exists anywhere in the matrix

readinessPolicy: readiness is false from every partially recovered crash state and from every quarantined or rejected rollback state; it is true only after the terminal-verification transition has durably landed

scopeLimits: W32 (demo/midgard-watcher/src/proof-state-machine.ts) and W33 (demo/midgard-watcher/src/submission-reconciliation.ts) are NOT_STARTED and their modules do not exist in the tree, so the seven-transition lifecycle is driven by a deterministic in-test driver over the real W03 durable record schema and the real W03 atomic journal boundary. The crash, restart, idempotence, referential-integrity, canonical-encoding and atomicity properties exercised are production properties; the transition sequencing policy is not yet owned by a production module.
The ordinary rollback, deep rollback and configured-source inconsistency cases drive the real W12/W13 production entry points with no in-test substitution.
